name: Evans Gambit
sac_idea: Sacrifice the b4 pawn on move 4 to gain rapid central development, open diagonals for the queen and bishop, and launch a furious attack against Black's king on f7.
why: A classic romantic gambit that immediately forces sharp, concrete tactical calculations and forces Black onto the defensive from move 4.

name: Fried Liver Attack
sac_idea: Sacrifice a knight on f7 (5.Nxf7!) to drag Black's king out into the open center, creating overwhelming attacking pressure with 6.Qf3+.
why: Exploits weak defended squares on f7 with devastating tactical violence when Black plays the naive 5...Nxd5.

name: Giuoco Piano: Göring / Center Attack
sac_idea: Push d4 early and sacrifice central pawns (c3/d4) for rapid piece development and open e-file/f-file assault lines.
why: Replaces passive Italian d3 setups with sharp, energetic piece activity and tactical initiative.

name: King's Gambit Accepted
sac_idea: Sacrifice the f2-f4 pawn on move 2 to dismantle Black's center, open the f-file for the rook after castling, and dominate the center with e4/d4.
why: The ultimate aggressive response to 1...e5, forcing immediate tactical fights where passive defensive play is punished.

name: Danish Gambit / Center Game
sac_idea: Sacrifice two pawns (2.d4 exd4 3.c3 dxc3 4.Bc4 cxb2 5.Bxb2) to align raking bishops pointing directly at Black's kingside.
why: Trading pawns for maximum development speed creates massive tactical threats before Black can castle.

name: Smith-Morra Gambit
sac_idea: Sacrifice 3.c3 against the Sicilian Defense to open the c-file and d-file for rooks while Black's pieces remain cramped.
why: Bypasses complex open Sicilian mainlines, seizing the initiative and dictating the tactical flow from move 3.

name: Scotch Gambit
sac_idea: Play 3.d4 exd4 4.Bc4, delaying pawn recapture to quickly castle and strike at Black's uncastled king with Ng5 or c3.
why: Blends dynamic center strikes with sharp kingside threats, avoiding slow maneuvering games.

name: Vienna Gambit
sac_idea: Play 2.Nc3 followed by 3.f4, combining King's Gambit themes with central knight control to catch Black unprepared.
why: A dangerous surprise weapon that leads to sharp tactical middlegames while retaining central stability.

name: Albin Countergambit
sac_idea: Counter-strike against 1.d4 d5 2.c4 with 2...e5!, sacrificing a pawn to plant a wedging pawn on d3 that paralyzes White's queenside.
why: Refuses dry Queen's Gambit positions and seizes the initiative as Black with sharp tactical traps (Lasker Trap).

name: Traxler Counterattack
sac_idea: Respond to White's 4.Ng5 with 4...Bc5!?, ignoring the fork on f7 to launch a ferocious sac assault on f2 with ...Bxf2+ and ...Nxe4+.
why: Turns a defensive nightmare into an explosive tactical counter-assault where White can easily get checkmated.

name: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav Attack
sac_idea: Fianchetto the dark-squared bishop, castle short, and launch a devastating exchange sac (...Rxc3!) to shatter White's queenside attack.
why: High-octane opposite-side castling race where the player with the sharper tactical vision wins.

name: King's Indian Defense: Mar del Plata
sac_idea: Lock the center with ...e5 and d5, then storm the kingside with ...f5-f4-g5-g4, sacrificing pawns to break open White's king position.
why: The premier aggressive response to 1.d4, trading space on the queenside for a lethal direct attack on White's king.
